title: Existence of the localized restriction and tensor package
statement: Fix schemes X,Y, a morphism f:X to Y, coefficient sheaf rings RY,RX and an isomorphism c:f-inverse RY isomorphic to RX. For every Global datum g and object V of Y.ProEt, the restriction and tensor fields of Local(f,RY,RX,c,g,V) exist: the two exact localized restrictions, the localized module operation and derived adjunction, both localized tensor models and shifts, the ordinary and derived tensor comparisons, and their restriction comparisons with shifts.

source.place: Tag 04J0; Cohomology on Sites, Tags 08FI, 0FN5 and 07A4; the restriction/tensor part of the local construction.

proof.text: Construct the actual ordinary localized operation, coefficient section equation, ordinary pure-unit tensor comparison and resolving-class preservation using localOrdinaryResolving_exists.

source.place: Tag 04J0; Cohomology on Sites, Tags 08FI, 0FN5 and 07A4; the restriction/tensor part of the local construction.

proof.text: For each restriction construct its exact Restriction data using localizedSystemExact and tensorOverIso. tensorOverIso_naturality gives naturality. K-flat restriction follows from ringedSite_restriction_exact_kflat; flatness of the terms follows by pulling a covering sieve and its local equational solutions to the slice. Restriction preserves coproducts through its faithful abelian-sheaf forgetful functor and the cocontinuous slice forgetful functor. Construct each slice tensor model and normalized shifts with tensorModelWithShifts_nonempty, and apply exactTensorComparison_exists to each restriction.

source.place: Tag 04J0; Cohomology on Sites, Tags 08FI, 0FN5 and 07A4; the restriction/tensor part of the local construction.

proof.text: Ordinary tensor naturality for the localized pullback follows from its pure-unit equation by module adjunction and pure-tensor extensionality. Apply exactTensorComparison_exists to construct its normalized tensor comparison and both shifts. operationDerivedAdjunction supplies the normalized counit and its shift for the actual derived adjunction.
